An '''arithmetic sequence''' is a [[number sequence]] where each term after the first is a fixed amount larger or smaller than the previous one.

== Formal definition ==

$(a_n)$ is an '''arithmetic sequence''' if:

$$
a_n=a_0+nd
$$

$d=a_{n}-a_{n-1},\, \forall n \ge 1$ is known as the '''common difference''' of the sequence.

== Properties ==

=== Partial sum: $S_m$ ===

The sum of first $m$ terms of a geometric sequence is known as its '''partial sum''' up to the $m$th term, denoted by $S_n$.

$$
S_n=\frac{a_1+a_n}{2}n
$$

=== Limit behaviour: $\lim_{m \to \infty}a_m$ ===

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! $d$
! $\lim_{m \to \infty}a_m$
|-
| $>0$
| $\infty$
|-
